bug_info.bug_desc: The command-FIFO-not-empty interrupt was generated by edge-detecting `cmdfifo_notempty`, the read-side not-empty output of the asynchronous command FIFO. This caused two failures: (1) `cmdfifo_notempty` rises as soon as the opcode byte is pushed during the SPI transaction, so the interrupt could assert before the address and payload for that transaction had been uploaded, allowing software to read an incomplete/coherent command set; (2) an edge detector only pulses on the 0-to-1 transition, so if the FIFO was already non-empty when another command was uploaded, no new interrupt event was produced and back-to-back uploads could be missed. The spec requires the command-FIFO notification event to be a single sys_clk pulse generated at chip-select deassertion when at least one command is present in the FIFO.
bug_info.fix_hint: Remove `cmdfifo_notempty` from the shared edge detector and shrink that detector to cover only the payload interrupts. Instead, generate a dedicated command-FIFO event: in `spid_upload`, set an `sck_cmdfifo_set` flag when `cmdfifo_wvalid && cmdfifo_wready`, clear it when the write-side FIFO depth is empty, latch this flag on the CSb clock, and in sys_clk create a one-cycle `sys_cmdfifo_set` pulse on `sys_csb_deasserted_pulse_i` when the latched flag is set. Use this pulse for `intr_upload_cmdfifo_not_empty` and connect the FIFO write-side depth (`wdepth_o`) to support the empty/clear condition.
